pluss::subsp::stats::ts::Sarima¶

Fits a seasonal ARIMA model by maximum likelihood, in the notation (p, d, q)(P, D, Q)s.

Signature¶

ts::SarimaFit ts::Sarima::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::SarimaOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});
ts::SarimaFit ts::Sarima::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const pluss::Series& x, const ts::SarimaOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

Construction¶

Sarima has no instances: it is a namespace for the static fit_mle, which returns a SarimaFit.

Methods¶

fit_mle¶

ts::SarimaFit ts::Sarima::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::SarimaOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});
ts::SarimaFit ts::Sarima::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const pluss::Series& x, const ts::SarimaOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

Fits the seasonal model (p, d, q)(P, D, Q)s: the regular and seasonal polynomials multiply, so a model with p = 1, P = 1, s = 12 has coefficients at lags 1, 12 and 13 (the lag-13 coefficient is the product of the other two, with its sign). Differencing is applied regularly d times and seasonally D times before the ARMA part is fitted. The form with x adds exogenous regressors as in Arima::fit_mle.

const pluss::Series& y

The observed series in time order (a vector or an n × 1 matrix).

const pluss::Series& x

Exogenous regressors: an n × k matrix (or a vector) with one row per observation of y.

const ts::SarimaOptions& options

Orders, season length, starting values and search settings; see SarimaOptions.

pluss::codem::Config cfg

Output configuration (dtype and platform of the returned series); the fit itself runs in double precision.

Returns. A SarimaFit wrapping an ArimaFit in core, with the same evaluation methods.

Errors. A seasonal order without s > 1 is rejected: seasonal_period must be > 1 for SARIMA terms. The effective sample must be longer than the number of parameters.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

A multiplicative seasonal autoregression with period 12: the regular and the seasonal coefficient are both recovered.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.to_vec<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  std::vector<double> x(240, 0.0);
  const auto e = noise(240);
  for (int t = 0; t < 240; ++t) {
    x[t] = e[t] + (t >= 1 ? 0.4 * x[t - 1] : 0.0) + (t >= 12 ? 0.5 * x[t - 12] : 0.0) - (t >= 13 ? 0.2 * x[t - 13] : 0.0);
  }
  const Series y = pluss::make_series(x, {240}, f64);
  ts::SarimaOptions options;
  options.p = 1;
  options.P = 1;
  options.s = 12;
  const auto fit = ts::Sarima::fit_mle(y, options);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "ar = " << fit.core.ar[0] << ", seasonal ar = " << fit.core.sar[0] << ", log-likelihood = " << fit.loglik(y) << "\n";
  show("forecast", fit.forecast(6, y));
}

Output

ar = 0.3452, seasonal ar = 0.4646, log-likelihood = -39.5228
forecast         0.2404   0.1413   0.0531   0.1265  -0.0459   0.2256

Example 2¶

An ‘airline’ model with regular and seasonal differencing and one moving-average term of each kind.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.to_vec<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  std::vector<double> x(240, 0.0);
  const auto e = noise(240);
  for (int t = 0; t < 240; ++t) {
    x[t] = e[t] + (t >= 1 ? 0.4 * x[t - 1] : 0.0) + (t >= 12 ? 0.5 * x[t - 12] : 0.0) - (t >= 13 ? 0.2 * x[t - 13] : 0.0);
  }
  const Series y = pluss::make_series(x, {240}, f64);
  ts::SarimaOptions options;
  options.p = 0;
  options.d = 1;
  options.q = 1;
  options.D = 1;
  options.Q = 1;
  options.s = 12;
  const auto fit = ts::Sarima::fit_mle(y, options);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "ma = " << fit.core.ma[0] << ", seasonal ma = " << fit.core.sma[0] << "\n";
}

Output

ma = -0.8244, seasonal ma = -0.7101

Example 3¶

Seasonal terms need a season length.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.to_vec<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = ar1(100, 0.5);
  ts::SarimaOptions options;
  options.P = 1;  // no season length given
  try {
    ts::Sarima::fit_mle(y, options);
  } catch (const std::exception&) {
    std::cout << "seasonal terms without s are rejected\n";
  }
}

Output

seasonal terms without s are rejected
